title: Smart Routing: add Hosted route canary split primitive (deterministic cohorting + region-aware enforcement)
author: Ravi Menon
description: Context: As part of Hosted canary rollouts GA work, we need a data-plane primitive that can split traffic on a Hosted route between a baseline target and a canary target by percentage, with deterministic cohort assignment (sticky per caller) and region-aware enforcement. This PR adds a new routing primitive `canary_split` to the Smart Routing evaluation + enforcement path. The primitive is intentionally minimal: it takes two compatible upstream targets (baseline + canary), a canary weight (0-100), and a deterministic cohort key, then selects the target for a request. This will be wired into the Rollout Orchestrator/control plane in follow-ups. What’s included: (1) New route config primitive `canary_split` with validation (weights must sum to 100, baseline/canary targets must be same modality and compatible model family; canary weight can be 0-100; guardrails around missing/invalid fields). (2) Deterministic cohorting: compute `cohort_bucket` = xxhash64(<cohort_key> + <route_id> + <rollout_id?>) mod 100; bucket < canary_weight => canary else baseline. If rollout_id is omitted we still include a stable config hash so cohorting does not flip on unrelated route config changes. (3) Cohort key derivation: prefer `x-redwood-cohort-key` header (set by gateway / console preview tools); fallback to API key id; final fallback to stable client IP hash when key id is unavailable (internal-only paths). We explicitly do NOT use request body content. (4) Region-aware behavior: the split is evaluated locally in each region using the same deterministic algorithm to preserve the global percentage distribution while avoiding cross-region coordination; we include region in logs but not in the hash input to avoid region-driven cohort flipping for clients that fail over. (5) Retries/streaming handling: we ensure the chosen target is pinned for the lifetime of a request (including internal retries) by storing `selected_target` in request context; for streaming requests we do not re-evaluate mid-stream. (6) Observability hooks: adds structured routing logs fields (`route_id`, `primitive=canary_split`, `cohort=baseline|canary`, `cohort_bucket`, `canary_weight`, `target_id`) and emits a low-cardinality counter `routing.canary_split.selected` with `cohort` and `region` tags only. Metric tagging with `rollout_id` is intentionally excluded here to avoid cardinality; it will be added at the gateway/telemetry layer where we can control aggregation (tracked in ENG-9152). (7) Safety: if validation fails or canary target is unhealthy/unavailable at evaluation time, we fall back to baseline and emit `routing.canary_split.fallback_to_baseline` with a reason code. Notes / decisions: - The deterministic hash input includes route_id to avoid cross-route correlation (same cohort key should not always land in canary across all routes). - We intentionally do not include region in the hash to preserve stickiness when a client fails over between regions. - This primitive does not implement auto-stop/rollback; it only selects a target. Control plane/orchestrator will adjust `canary_weight` and state transitions. Test plan: - Unit tests for validation + cohorting distribution (bucket boundaries, 0/100%, stable behavior). - Integration tests in `smart-routing-sim` to confirm selection is pinned across retries and streaming. - Manual in staging: configure a test Hosted route with 10% canary split; send requests with fixed `x-redwood-cohort-key` and observe consistent cohort selection + logs. Rollout plan: - This ships behind `routing.enable_canary_split_primitive` flag (default off). - Console/orchestrator will not emit this primitive until backend support is enabled tenant-by-tenant. Follow-ups: - Wire `rollout_id` + cohort tags end-to-end at gateway/telemetry (ENG-9152). - Console preview + validation endpoint to render the split plan (part of orchestrator/console backend PR). - Guardrail policy enforcement (max step, soak) is out of scope here (policy engine).

smart-routing: implement deterministic cohorting (xxhash64) + request context pinning
smart-routing: add region-aware enforcement + fallback to baseline on errors
obs: add routing logs fields + low-cardinality counter for cohort selection

review_conversation: Mina Haddad: Please confirm whether including region in the hash input would cause cohort flips on failover. I think we should not include it.
Ravi Menon (author): Agree. I removed region from the hash input and added an explicit comment + test case for failover stickiness.
Emily Zhao: How do we ensure retries don’t bounce between baseline/canary if the gateway replays the request?
Ravi Menon (author): We pin `selected_target` in request context after first evaluation and reuse it for internal retries; added an integration test covering 2 retries with forced upstream 502.
Zachary Hill: Validation: do we need to enforce baseline/canary compatibility (same modality / model family)? Otherwise we may route chat -> embeddings accidentally.
Ravi Menon (author): Added a compatibility check in validator: both targets must have matching `target_type` and `interface` fields; rejects mismatches with a clear error.
Allison Grant: Metric cardinality: please avoid tagging with route_id/rollout_id for now; we can add cohort selection counts but keep tags bounded.
Ravi Menon (author): Done. Metrics use only `cohort` and `region`. Route/target info is in structured logs.
Ethan Park: Can we make the hash input stable across unrelated config changes? If config hash changes often, cohort assignments will churn.
Ravi Menon (author): Updated: we use route_id + (explicit rollout_id if present else `split_config_stability_key`). The stability key is derived from baseline/canary target ids + weights only.
Mina Haddad: Looks good. Please add a flag gate and default off.
Ravi Menon (author): Added `routing.enable_canary_split_primitive` with default false and documented expected enablement flow.
Emily Zhao: Approved after retry pinning test landed.
release_notes: Internal: Adds `canary_split` routing primitive for Hosted routes (behind feature flag). Enables deterministic baseline/canary traffic splitting in the data plane; control plane/orchestrator wiring in follow-ups.
